hints: Look carefully at each C=C double bond and check whether the two groups on each carbon are different enough for cis-trans isomerism.
Notice the left-hand double bond has two identical methyl groups on one carbon, while the middle double bond has two different groups on each carbon.

walkthrough:
**Check each double bond for cis-trans isomerism**

Look for a C=C where each carbon has two different groups attached. That is the only type that can show cis-trans isomerism.

Rule:
$$\text{cis-trans possible only if } C_a(X)(Y)=C_b(P)(Q) \text{ with } X \neq Y \text{ and } P \neq Q$$

**Count the cis-trans isomers of geranyl ethanoate**

The left C=C is $(CH_3)_2C=CH-$. One carbon has two identical $CH_3$ groups, so no cis-trans isomerism there. The middle C=C is $-CH_2CH_2C(CH_3)=CHCH_2O-$. Each carbon has two different groups, so it can be cis or trans.

So there is only 1 isomerisable double bond:
$$\text{number of isomers} = 2^1 = 2$$

**Work out the bromination product X**

With excess bromine, each alkene undergoes electrophilic addition. The ester $C=O$ does not react.

$$\text{-CH=C- + Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{-CHBr-CBr-}$$

**Count chiral centres in X**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups. After addition we get four new C-Br carbons.

Left alkene: $(CH_3)_2CBr-CHBr-$ gives one chiral centre at $CHBr$, but the $CBr(CH_3)_2$ carbon has two identical $CH_3$ groups so is not chiral. Middle alkene: $-CBr(CH_3)-CHBr-$ gives two chiral centres, as both carbons have four different groups. Total is 1 + 2 = 3 chiral centres.

options.A: Correct. Only the middle C=C can show cis-trans isomerism, giving 2 isomers including geranyl ethanoate itself. After addition of 2 molecules of $Br_2$, X has 3 chiral centres, one from the left double bond and two from the middle double bond.
options.B: Close but not quite. The 2 cis-trans isomers is correct, but 4 chiral centres is too many. It wrongly counts the $CBr(CH_3)_2$ carbon as chiral, forgetting that two identical methyl groups means it cannot have four different groups.
options.C: The 3 chiral centres is correct, but 4 cis-trans isomers is too many. It wrongly assumes both C=C bonds can show cis-trans isomerism, forgetting the left $(CH_3)_2C=$ bond has two identical groups on one carbon.
options.D: Both numbers are too high. It counts both double bonds as isomerisable to get 2^2 = 4, and counts all four brominated carbons as chiral. Both errors come from missing the effect of the two identical methyl groups on the left-hand end.
